//profiler_raw_window_points: Bounds the raw pass's response, not its rows: the read is one wide row per message carrying one value per variable, so this figure is divided by the variables read (floored at 2000 rows) and the applied number is recorded in the profile as raw_window.row_limit.
//postgres: Empty runs the in-memory stores. A per-user LLM spend cap is then only as old as the process, so set this before relying on one (SPEC §3.3).
//llm: Any subset of the four providers of SPEC §5.7. With none configured, ODE serves M0-M2 and no chat. Keys belong in the environment, not here.
//claude_cli: A development convenience for working without an API key. Reaches ODE's tools over MCP, so it needs public_url to be set.
//llm_pricing: Per million tokens, for the estimated cost SPEC §3.3 accounts against. Matched exactly, else by longest prefix. Not baked into the binary: published prices change, and a stale figure makes a cost cap quietly wrong. Verify before relying on these.
//jupyterhub: SPEC §5.6. Empty leaves the kernel surface unserved. The token is ODE's JupyterHub *service* credential and must hold servers, tokens, access:servers and users:activity — startup fails if it does not. See deploy/jupyterhub/ for the values that grant them. The workspace path is relative to the singleuser server root and has to be inside the mounted PVC, which this chart puts at ~/data rather than over the whole home.
//tool_bounds: The first two bound one projection; the next two bound a whole response. tool_quick_token_budget is what a ranked candidate list may cost the model, tool_profile_max_profiles how many full profiles one profile_series answer carries. Raise them and every tool call carries the difference for the rest of the turn.
//charts: SPEC §5.9. chart_max_points bounds one series of one chart: the aggregation bucket is widened until the window fits it, so this trades resolution against the size of the read and never truncates the window. chart_default_lookback is what a chart covers when neither the author nor a named profile says.
//relations: SPEC §5.5. relation_max_members bounds one relational pass; the pair count grows with the square of it and the rule count with four times that, so this bounds how readable the rule list is rather than how expensive the read is — the aligned read is one batched query either way. relation_max_buckets bounds the aligned grid, which is widened to fit rather than shortening the window. relation_default_lookback is a month rather than a week because an exception at certain times of day needs several samples in each hour bucket of each weekday. relation_max_graph_neighbours bounds how far out of the requested aspect a device relationship graph may pull: a graph of a whole site names hundreds of devices, and each one outside the aspect costs a device read, so this is what keeps one room's question from becoming a site survey.
//tool_run_code: Far smaller than jupyterhub_max_output_bytes above, and for a different cost: that one bounds a developer's console, this one bounds what a cell's output costs in model context.
